# Isaac Lab absolute IK is usable on default base, but drifts after rotating 90 degrees; how does the original thread and merged PR handle this?

> **Current answer:** Align the target, error, and Jacobian reference coordinate system. The old DifferentialInverseKinematicsAction directly used the world-frame geometric Jacobian, but solved for the root/base-frame target; the author separately left-multiplied the linear and angular velocity blocks of the Jacobian by the base rotation matrix and restored stable control on the rotated base. The merged PR #967 incorporates this transformation into the action and distinguishes between world-frame and base-frame Jacobians. Absolute targets from the world frame must also be converted by the calling side or the action, following the same convention.

## Key terms

- Geometric Jacobian (几何雅可比)
- Base frame (基座坐标系)
- World frame (世界坐标系)
- Batched matrix multiplication (批量矩阵乘法)
- Differential inverse kinematics (微分逆运动学)

## Problem and symptoms

- When the absolute IK is on the robot's base and not rotated, it can track, but after rotating 90 degrees, it continues to drift; how should the target and Jacobian reference frame be verified?
- A constant base-frame target is stable in the default base, but the end effector drifts after the base is rotated 90 degrees.
- The initial position and pose errors are close to zero, but the control process still drifts.

## Environment

- Isaac Lab commit 7452386; Isaac Sim 4.1; Ubuntu 20.04; RTX 4090; CUDA 12.5; Franka IK-Abs task.

## Priority diagnostics

- The action target, current end-effector pose, and Jacobian reference frame are all marked, and one should not only look at the initial error vector.
- The maintainer clarified that the PhysX Jacobian itself can be legally located in the world frame; the issue lies in the DifferentialInverseKinematicsAction needing to be consistent with the root/base-frame target.
- quat_apply only accepts N×3 vectors, but the Jacobian block is N×3×n_Dof; the thread confirms that matrix_from_quat and torch.bmm should be used.

## Possible causes

- The old implementation did not read the root/base pose to convert the geometric Jacobian, leading to Jacobian inconsistency with the target/error frame when the base is rotated.

## Attempts

- The author used inverse(base_quat) to generate a 3×3 rotation matrix, performed batched matrix multiplication on the linear and angular velocity blocks of the Jacobian, and demonstrated stable remote operation on a base rotated 90 degrees.
- The contributor further discussed that if the absolute target is given in the world frame, it must be converted to the base frame; the thread explicitly states this is an interface design choice, and the calling side must maintain consistency.

## Effective fixes

- Use the version containing PR #967; this PR in DifferentialInverseKinematicsAction moves the Jacobian to the root frame and distinguishes between world-frame and base-frame Jacobian attributes.
- In the old version, the base rotation matrix was used to left-multiply the linear and angular velocity blocks of the Jacobian, and the absolute target was converted to the same base/root frame.

## Result

- The author demonstrated the fix on a Franka base rotated 90 degrees, showing stable remote operation; PR #967 has been merged, with a merge commit of 762f4e32, and the Issue is closed.

## Limitations

- The world-frame Jacobian is not inherently an error; it must be converted only when the controller error and command use root/base frame.
- PR #967's test checklist is not fully completed, and regression testing on other robots should still be performed.

## Safety notes

- Before real machine movement, at least two non-zero base orientations should be used to validate the same end-effector target, and the frame name should be recorded; zero orientation testing cannot expose such coordinate system errors.
